home_tract: Rohtak, Jind, Hisar, Bhiwani, and Fatehabad districts
coat_colour: Jet black; occasional small white markings on face and switch of tail
horn_characteristics: Tightly curled horns ('Jalebi' curl) turning backwards, upwards and spiraling inwards
body_characteristics: Massive, wedge-shaped dairy conformation, deep body, long neck, short legs
milk_information: World's premier dairy buffalo breed with high lactation yields and 7-8% butterfat (Avg: 2,205 kg per lactation)
description: The undisputed 'Black Gold' of Indian dairying, Murrah is the premier dairy buffalo breed in the world, famed for high yields and tightly curled horns.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Ferozepur, Fazilka, Amritsar, and Gurdaspur districts along Sutlej and Ravi rivers
coat_colour: Predominantly black with distinctive white markings on forehead, face, muzzle, legs, and tail ('Panjkalyan')
horn_characteristics: Small, tightly curled horns similar to Murrah but slightly more compact
body_characteristics: Deep, wedge-shaped frame, fine neck, wide hips, and well-developed udder
milk_information: High dairy yield, close rival to Murrah in milk volume and fat content (Avg: 1,950 kg per lactation)
description: Celebrated dairy buffalo breed of Punjab, recognized by its distinctive 'Panjkalyan' five white markings and wall eyes.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Agra, Etawah (UP) and Bhind, Morena (MP) in the Chambal river ravines
coat_colour: Copper / wheat-straw colour, lighter shades on ventral side
horn_characteristics: Sword-shaped horns curving backward, upward, and slightly inward
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, wedge-shaped, active body with strong legs and tough hooves
milk_information: World-famous for the highest milk fat percentage among all buffalo breeds (up to 8.5% - 13%) (Avg: 1,220 kg per lactation)
description: Famed copper-colored buffalo of the Chambal ravines, holding the world record for the highest butterfat content in milk.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Mehsana, Banaskantha, Sabarkantha, Patan, and Gandhinagar districts
horn_characteristics: Intermediate between Murrah and Surti; irregular curve backwards and upwards with less tight curl
body_characteristics: Long, massive, deep-bodied with wedge-shaped dairy conformation
milk_information: Outstanding commercial milker with long continuous lactation and short inter-calving interval (Avg: 1,988 kg per lactation)
description: Premier commercial dairy buffalo of northern Gujarat evolved from Murrah and Surti crosses, famed for prolonged lactation persistence.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Kheda, Anand, Vadodara, Bharuch, and Surat districts
coat_colour: Black or rusty brown; skin is dark grey to copper red
horn_characteristics: Flat, sickle-shaped horns curving downward, backward, and then upward to form a hook
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, well-shaped, compact body with straight back and clean head
milk_information: High milk fat percentage (7.5-8.5%) and economical feed conversion (Avg: 1,667 kg per lactation)
description: Medium-sized dairy buffalo of the Charotar tract of Gujarat, recognized by characteristic sickle-shaped horns and two white neck collars.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Gir forest and Kathiawar peninsula: Junagadh, Bhavnagar, Amreli, Porbandar, Rajkot
horn_characteristics: Heavy, broad, flat horns drooping down along the sides of the neck and then turning upwards in an inclined curl
body_characteristics: Massive, heaviest buffalo breed in India, deep long barrel, heavy bones and strong muscular neck
milk_information: High milk producer with very high butterfat percentage (8-10%) (Avg: 2,239 kg per lactation)
description: The heaviest Indian buffalo breed, originating in the Gir forests, famous for massive down-drooping horns, bulging forehead, and rich milk.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Nagpur, Wardha, Chandrapur, Amravati, Akola, and Yavatmal districts
coat_colour: Black; white patches occasionally seen on face, legs, and tail switch
horn_characteristics: Long, flat, sword-shaped horns curving backward on each side of the neck reaching nearly to the shoulders
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, light-boned, athletic, clean-limbed body
milk_information: Good dairy yield under low-input farming systems (Avg: 1,055 kg per lactation)
description: Prominent dual-purpose buffalo of Vidarbha with long sword-like horns, celebrated for working under extreme dry heat without wallowing.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Solapur, Sangli, Satara, and Kolhapur districts along the Bhima river basin
coat_colour: Usually black, occasionally light black or brownish
horn_characteristics: Very long, flat horns extending backwards, up to 45-50 inches, sometimes touching the pin bones
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, compact, long slender barrel with thin neck and prominent eyes
milk_information: High dairy yield with regular calving intervals (12-13 months) (Avg: 1,450 kg per lactation)
description: Famous dairy buffalo of southern Maharashtra, recognizable by its extraordinarily long backwards-sweeping horns and regular calving cycle.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Beed, Parbhani, Nanded, Latur, Hingoli, and Jalna districts
horn_characteristics: Long, flat horns extending parallel to neck backwards, turning slightly upward at tips
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, compact body with straight back and strong limbs
milk_information: Moderate milk yield under drought and fodder scarcity (Avg: 1,115 kg per lactation)
description: Hardy dual-purpose buffalo of the Marathwada region, valued for consistent milk production and draught under recurrent drought.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Nilgiris district (high-altitude plateau around Ooty)
coat_colour: Fawn, ash-grey, or silver-grey; thick dense hairy coat with dark markings
horn_characteristics: Long, wide crescent horns emerging outwards and curving inwards to form a wide semicircle
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, thick-set, stocky, long barrel, with dense hair along back and chest
milk_information: High butterfat milk (around 8%), central to the sacred dairy rituals of Toda temples (Avg: 500 kg per lactation)
description: Sacred, semi-wild buffalo of the Toda tribe in the high Nilgiris, famed for wide crescent horns, ash-grey coat, and cold tolerance.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Kutch district (Banni grasslands and Rann of Kutch fringes)
horn_characteristics: Medium-sized, coiled horns curving backwards, upwards and spiraling tightly into a ring
body_characteristics: Medium to large, compact, deep-bodied, robust frame with strong legs
milk_information: Exceptional milk yield under night-grazing range systems in arid grasslands (Avg: 2,857 kg per lactation)
description: Celebrated dairy buffalo of the Kutch desert reared by Maldhari pastoralists, known for unique nocturnal grazing and high milk yields.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Puri, Khurda, and Ganjam districts surrounding the Chilika lagoon
horn_characteristics: Curved backwards, upwards, and slightly inwards with pointed tips
body_characteristics: Small to medium, compact, hardy, agile body with strong hooves
milk_information: Cows yield rich, thick milk with 8-9% fat, traditionally made into famous Chilika curd (Avg: 500 kg per lactation)
description: World-unique buffalo breed of the Chilika lagoon in Odisha, famous for nocturnal aquatic swimming and foraging on saline macrophytes.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Kalahandi and Rayagada districts
horn_characteristics: Long, flat horns curving backward, outward and slightly upward
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, sturdy, well-knit body with strong legs
milk_information: Moderate milk yield under forest grazing systems (Avg: 760 kg per lactation)
description: Indigenous buffalo of the Kalahandi hills of Odisha, maintained by local farmers for dual milk and agricultural tillage.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Brahmaputra and Barak river basins in Assam and valleys of Manipur
coat_colour: Dark grey to black, occasionally with two white chevron markings on neck
horn_characteristics: Wide crescent horns emerging outward and curving backward and upward in a flat plane
body_characteristics: Stocky, compact, deep body with short muscular legs and large round hooves for mud traction
milk_information: Low milk yield (1 to 2.5 litres daily), primarily kept for draught and meat (Avg: 385 kg per lactation)
description: First registered swamp buffalo breed of India, recognized for 2n=48 chromosomes, broad hooves, and powerful puddling in marshy wetlands.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Bargur hills in Anthiyur taluk of Erode district
horn_characteristics: Curved backwards, upwards, and slightly inwards with sharp tips
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, compact, agile, muscular body adapted to hill climbing
milk_information: Low to moderate milk yield under forest grazing (Avg: 480 kg per lactation)
description: Hill buffalo breed reared by the Lingayat community in the Bargur hills of Tamil Nadu, known for agility in mountain terrain.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Raipur, Bilaspur, Durg, Rajnandgaon, and Janjgir-Champa districts
horn_characteristics: Curved backwards and outwards with upward tips
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, well-proportioned body with strong legs
milk_information: Moderate dairy yield under rural agro-pastoral feeding (Avg: 920 kg per lactation)
description: Prominent dual-purpose buffalo of the Chhattisgarh plains, indispensable for rice puddle tillage and household milk production.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Rupnagar, Hoshiarpur (Punjab) and Kangra, Chamba, Una, Bilaspur (HP)
coat_colour: Black or dark brown with white markings on face and legs in many animals
horn_characteristics: Medium, curved backwards and upwards into a semi-circle
body_characteristics: Medium to large, robust, deep-bodied with strong muscular limbs
milk_information: Good dairy yield under mobile migratory feeding by Gujjars (Avg: 1,250 kg per lactation)
description: Migratory pastoral buffalo of the Shivalik foothills and Himachal hills, maintained by pastoral Gujjars for rich milk and ghee.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Dharwad, Belgaum, Bagalkot, Gadag, and Haveri districts
horn_characteristics: Curved backwards, upwards, and slightly inwards
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, compact body, straight back, clean head
milk_information: Good milk yield with high total solids, ideal for sweet and curd preparation (Avg: 1,180 kg per lactation)
description: Indigenous dairy buffalo of northern Karnataka, famous for rich milk with high total solids used to make the GI-tagged Dharwad Peda.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Koraput, Malkangiri, and Nabarangpur districts
coat_colour: Ash grey or brown with copper tint; hair often golden-yellow at tips
horn_characteristics: Broad, flat horns curving backwards and upwards in a broad crescent
body_characteristics: Small to medium, sturdy, muscular body with strong legs
milk_information: Modest milk yield with high fat content under forest foraging (Avg: 600 kg per lactation)
description: Indigenous buffalo of the Koraput plateau of Odisha, bred by tribal farmers for resilient draught and nutrient-rich milk.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Akola, Amravati, and Buldhana districts along the Purna river basin
horn_characteristics: Flat, sword-shaped horns curving backwards along the neck
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, well-built, compact body with straight back
milk_information: Good dairy yield with high fat content under dryland feeding (Avg: 1,150 kg per lactation)
description: Hardy dual-purpose buffalo of the Purna river valley in Vidarbha, adapted to saline water and deep black cotton soil tillage.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Dhubri, Goalpara, and South Salmara-Mankachar districts along Brahmaputra river
horn_characteristics: Curved backwards, outwards, and upwards
body_characteristics: Medium to large, deep-bodied, robust frame with wide ribs
milk_information: Moderate to good milk yield under riverine wetland grazing (Avg: 820 kg per lactation)
description: Indigenous buffalo of the lower Brahmaputra valley in Assam, renowned for remarkable swimming endurance and wetland tillage.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: Amravati district (Melghat forest hills)
coat_colour: Black or dark grey with occasional reddish tinge
horn_characteristics: Flat horns curving backwards and upwards along the neck
body_characteristics: Medium-sized, compact, stocky body with strong limbs and tough hooves
milk_information: Low to moderate milk yield under forest grazing (Avg: 710 kg per lactation)
description: Hardy indigenous buffalo of the Melghat hills of Maharashtra, reared by tribal Gaoli communities for forest grazing and hill agriculture.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)

home_tract: North Goa and South Goa districts
horn_characteristics: Curved backwards, upwards, and slightly inwards
body_characteristics: Small to medium, compact, hardy, low-set body with sturdy legs
milk_information: Modest milk yield with rich fat percentage (Avg: 640 kg per lactation)
description: Indigenous buffalo breed of Goa officially recognized by ICAR-NBAGR, adapted to humid coastal farming and Khazan land cultivation.
official_source: ICAR - National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR)
